title: The Artist Whose Work Has Killed Nearly 1 Million Animals
description: A look at Damien Hirst's controversial art career, including the infamous shark-in-formaldehyde piece, and the staggering number of animals used across his work. Original AI-narrated commentary, not affiliated with the artist.

hook_candidates.text: One artist's work has cost nearly a million animals their lives — and sold for millions of dollars.
What if one artist's most famous piece cost nearly a million animals their lives?
You'd think buying expensive art is harmless. This artist's body of work says otherwise.
In the 1990s, a British artist caught a tiger shark, dropped it in formaldehyde, and sold it for millions — that was just the beginning.

beats.text: His name is Damien Hirst, and his most famous piece is a tiger shark suspended in a tank of formaldehyde.
beats.broll_query: shark suspended formaldehyde tank art installation

beats.text: That single shark sold for eight million dollars — even after it started to rot and had to be replaced.
The shark's just one piece — estimates put his total animal use above nine hundred thousand, mostly insects, but also sheep and cows.
Critics call it shock value. Collectors call it visionary.
Either way, it's some of the most expensive art of the last fifty years — built entirely from dead animals.
